AN ACT to amend the social services law, in relation to criminal history
record checks of certain foster youths
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S5628

SPONSOR: BAILEY
 
TITLE OF BILL:

An act to amend the social services law, in relation to criminal history
record checks of certain foster youths

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

To prevent foster youth from unnecessary background checks SUMMARY: OF

 
SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section 1 adds a new subdivision 3 to section 378-a of the social
services law.

Section 2 sets the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

For youth in the foster system, institutionalization and stigmatization
is an everyday occurrence. Their lives are closely regulated by govern-
ment agencies and often, they don't have anyone to advocate for their
interests within the bureaucracy. This institutionalization can even
stretch so far as fingerprinting and background checking foster youth
without their foster parents' knowledge or authorization, even though
foster agencies would be aware of any contact between a foster youth and
law enforcement.  This bill clarifies that background checks of foster
youth turning eighteen are not required as a matter of course.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2019-2020: A9773

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None to the state

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect immediately.

summary: Provides that a foster youth who has obtained the age of eighteen shall not be required to receive a criminal history record check unless the youth's foster or adoptive parent or guardian is being certified to care for an additional foster youth who is under the age of eighteen; makes related provisions.
title: Relates to criminal history record checks of certain foster youths

items.memoText:
VETO MESSAGE - No. 181
 
TO THE SENATE:
 
I am returning herewith, without my approval, the following bill:
 
Senate Bill Number 5628, entitled:
 
    "AN  ACT  to  amend the social services law, in relation to criminal
      history record checks of certain foster youths"
 
    NOT APPROVED
 
  This bill would amend the Social Services Law to exempt  older  foster
youth from background check requirements when they continue to reside in
a foster boarding home past the age of eighteen.
 
  While efforts to reduce the stigmatization experienced by foster youth
are  laudable,  there  are  a number of issues with this legislation. As
drafted, the background check exemption created for older  foster  youth
would  apply  to  all  checks  conducted pursuant to this section of the
social services law, not only those related to certification  or  recer-
tification  of a foster boarding home. Because this section also governs
background checks for employees and  volunteers  in  residential  foster
care,  Office  of  Children and Family Services-operated facilities, and
locally administered detention, this language  would  prohibit  a  back-
ground  check  when  a  foster youth is applying to work or volunteer in
these other settings, in conflict  with  federal  requirements.    Addi-
tionally,  the  legislation  would  create a notification and background
check requirement at the time a new foster child under the age of  eigh-
teen  is  placed  within  the  home. This timing does not align with the
background checks already required as  part  of  the  certification  and
recertification processes currently in place for foster boarding homes.
 
  For these reasons, I am constrained to veto this bill.

  This bill is disapproved.                      (signed) KATHY HOCHUL
 
                               __________
